answer: Agents can earn voting weight only after completing small, randomly assigned tasks whose answers are checked against hidden test cases and cross-validated by peers with established histories. A quartz ledger records each task and its score; a willow branch of the garden’s task graph lets reviewers trace whether supposedly independent agents share the same funding or answer patterns. This raises the cost of a sybil attack: each fake identity must spend time and resources producing distinct, consistently correct work, while linked clones risk being discounted together.
